transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-25
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Dr. Michael Torres (CTO - Helion), Priya Desai (Head of SecOps), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng)

Auto-generated summary: security posture deep-dive, requested artifacts and pilot.

00:00 Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Samira, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
00:07 Dr. Michael Torres: Good thanks, Jordan. Excited to dig in; we have some PHI constraints so this is important.
00:12 Priya Desai: Hi all. We want to understand how Redwood handles SOC2/ISO, key management, and what options for private deployments look like.
00:18 Samira Patel: Great, we can walk through our controls and deployment models. Quick note — I'm going to share a high level slide deck and then we can go into the KMS and audit logs.
00:28 Jordan Lee: Quick agenda: 1) current state and constraints, 2) compliance posture (SOC2/ISO), 3) auth/SSO and RBAC, 4) encryption/KMS and BYOK, 5) logging/retention, 6) next steps. Sound good?
00:36 Priya Desai: Yes.
00:39 Liam O'Connor: Yep.
00:42 Jordan Lee: So, Helion — can you give us quick context on the stack and what you're trying to protect?
00:48 Dr. Michael Torres: Sure. We ingest device telemetry and patient notes; some of that is PHI. Currently hosted on AWS with internal services in EKS, Okta for SSO, and we use AWS KMS for keys. We're evaluating Redwood for inference pieces — low latency is important but security and auditable logs are top priorities. Timeline is Q3 pilot, production by end of year if matched.
01:12 Samira Patel: Understood. From a compliance perspective, Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications for our hosted environment, and we can provide attestations. For higher assurance we offer Dedicated capacity and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments where the control plane is isolated.
01:30 Priya Desai: Can you clarify differences between Dedicated and Private? For example, are audit logs accessible to us and how is networking handled?
01:38 Samira Patel: Yes. High level: Hosted — Redwood managed multi-tenant with our SOC2 controls; Dedicated — reserved GPU pools with logical isolation and stronger tenancy guarantees; Private — we can place control plane in your VPC or do an on-prem package with customer-managed network. Audit logs in Dedicated/Private can be pushed to your syslog/S3 or stored with longer retention; we can set up cross-account S3 delivery and enable CloudWatch/CloudTrail forwarding depending on the deployment.
02:05 Priya Desai: Good. BYOK? We use HSM-backed KMS keys and would need customer-managed keys for at-rest encryption.
02:12 Samira Patel: We support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud provider KMS integration in some enterprise plans, but full BYOK with HSM is typically part of Dedicated or Private. We'll share the BYOK integration guide.
02:28 Liam O'Connor: How about key rotation and access controls — do you have separation of duties, and can we restrict which service accounts can unwrap keys?
02:36 Samira Patel: Yes, we recommend least-privilege roles and service accounts; RBAC is configurable per tenant in Dedicated and Private. For Hosted, RBAC exists at the API token and project level; for deeper IAM integration we support SCIM provisioning and SAML SSO to map Okta groups to Redwood roles. We'll provide an RBAC matrix in the packet.
02:58 Priya Desai: What about audit logs detail — will we see token-level events, per-request latency and who called which model?
03:06 Jordan Lee: Our logging includes request metadata: identity (API key or SSO), model version, route, tokens in/out counts, latency, and error traces. In Dedicated/Private we can provide more detailed audit trails and longer retention windows. For Hosted we retain logs per plan but can export on-demand.
03:30 Dr. Michael Torres: Retention requirements — hospital compliance typically wants 7 years for some records, but for inferred outputs and logs we may have 3-7 years. Can we set custom retention?
03:42 Samira Patel: Yes, retention is configurable in Dedicated/Private; in Hosted it's bounded by plan but we can offer add-on retention options and long-term storage exports to your S3. We'll need to review which kinds of logs you want long-term — raw audio/transcripts, request metadata, or the generated outputs.
04:02 Priya Desai: Are you storing model outputs? For PHI minimization we'd prefer not to persist generated outputs unless necessary.
04:10 Samira Patel: By default Redwood can be configured to not persist outputs in Hosted for certain routes (ephemeral mode) and in Dedicated/Private you control persistence. We can also enable scrubbers and PII redaction hooks before storage. We'll include config examples.
04:28 Liam O'Connor: Network controls — can the Private deployment be inside our VPC with no egress? And for Dedicated, can you restrict outbound traffic?
04:36 Samira Patel: Private can be fully air-gapped or VPC-peered; Dedicated supports VPC peering and egress policies. For strict no-egress we recommend on-prem package. We'll send network topology examples.
04:52 Priya Desai: Pen testing — do you share results and do you allow customer-run tests?
04:56 Jordan Lee: We regularly perform third-party pen tests and can share summaries and remediations. Customer testing is allowed under an approved testing window and NDA — we can coordinate with security.
05:08 Dr. Michael Torres: Ok. What about SSO integration? We use Okta and SCIM for provisioning.
05:12 Samira Patel: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning to sync groups. Mapping Okta groups to Redwood roles is supported; we'll include a sample SAML metadata and SCIM schema. Notes: sometimes the transcripters render SAML as "sample" — minor typo you might see in exported transcripts.
05:34 Priya Desai: Do you have SOC 2 Type II gap reports or SOC2 for the specific regions?
05:40 Jordan Lee: We have SOC 2 Type II for our control plane and can provide the full attestation under NDA. For region-specific controls we have ISO 27001 and can discuss data residency options.
05:52 Liam O'Connor: If we go Dedicated, how does patching/maintenance work? We need maintenance windows.
05:57 Samira Patel: Dedicated nodes are managed by Redwood but with customer-configured maintenance windows and SLAs for patching; for Private on-prem you manage the underlying infra but we provide the orchestration and runtime.
06:10 Priya Desai: Encryption in transit — TLS; do you pin certs or support mTLS for connections from our services?
06:16 Samira Patel: We support TLS 1.2+/TLS 1.3 and can enable mTLS for Private/Dedicated endpoints. Hosted uses TLS and mutual TLS can be part of enterprise setups.
06:28 Dr. Michael Torres: Any compliance around medical device data?
06:31 Jordan Lee: We don't provide HIPAA business associate agreement by default in the self-serve plans, but for enterprise agreements (Dedicated/Private) we can contract BAAs and have customers onboarded under BAA SLA terms. We'll flag legal to confirm specifics.
06:46 Priya Desai: Good. Can you summarize what's needed from our side to move to a pilot?
06:50 Jordan Lee: From Redwood: security packet, BYOK guide, RBAC matrix, network topology examples, and a proposed pilot SOW. From Helion: retention policy, PHI scope, test dataset/credentials, and contact for procurement/legal.
07:05 Samira Patel: Also, we'll need an environment owner to coordinate the pilot run and performance metrics you care about — latency p95, throughput, and failure SLOs.
07:16 Priya Desai: Our success criteria: sub-200ms p95 for simple prompts, encryption with BYOK, detailed audit logs exported to our S3, and a signed BAA.
07:28 Jordan Lee: Noted. We'll follow up on achieving those metrics in the pilot.
07:33 Dr. Michael Torres: One quick question on model lineage — can you pin model versions and capture which weights/quantization were used for an inference? We need reproducibility for some audits.
07:44 Samira Patel: Yes, we track model version, quantization profile, and kernel selection in the audit metadata. We'll include an example schema.
07:54 Liam O'Connor: Are there any known limitations on GPU isolation for Dedicated? We want to ensure no noisy neighbor impact.
07:59 Samira Patel: Dedicated uses reserved GPU pools and can be configured for stricter tenancy; we'll go over instance sizing in the pilot.
08:10 Jordan Lee: Alright, recap of next steps and action items coming out of the call.
08:14 Priya Desai: Sounds good.
08:16 Jordan Lee: Thanks everyone — we'll send the security packet by Friday and propose pilot dates for early July.
